# Real AI game builds: workflows, playable demos, and complete source

Primary sources reviewed on 2026-10-18. Featured cases require a creator-provided record of AI involvement, a playable or locally runnable game, and the actual game project. AI contribution is attributed to those records; it is not an independently measured percentage. Study steps are GameMap editorial guidance.

44 reviewed cases: **28 2D** and **16 3D**; 37 browser links and 7 local downloads.

## Search scope and selection

Discovery covered public GitHub projects, creator sites, itch.io and game-jam pages, Hacker News and Reddit posts, and English, Chinese, and Japanese search terms for AI-built 2D/3D games, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Copilot. Community lists are discovery leads; each counted case links primary author evidence and its actual game source.

A README AI disclosure is labeled separately from a prompt, transcript, development log, or tutorial. Some entries are prototypes. A collection is counted as one case unless its individual games have separately reviewed gameplay and source. Browser access is checked where practical; download entries state their setup requirements, and known unavailable hosts are disclosed. Screenshots identify GameMap captures or creator-published gameplay, with provenance in the media guide. This is a growing reviewed collection, not an exhaustive inventory of every community game or a claim that all games were fully reproduced.

## Cloud Crush: Gemini CLI builds a match-3 game

Match cloud-service icons on an eight-by-eight board, chase a timed high score, and create special Gemini gems. Google publishes the complete Go game alongside a detailed Gemini CLI codelab.

**AI workflow:** Google’s repository attributes game generation to Gemini CLI. The official codelab shows human orchestration through plan mode, steering prompts, browser adaptation, testing, and subagents. That is publisher evidence, not an independent measurement of autonomous authorship.

- [See Google’s explicit Gemini CLI attribution](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/devrel-demos/blob/main/codelabs/gemini-cli/gemini-cli-match3-golang/README.md) — The publisher README explicitly names Gemini CLI; the separate official codelab records the development prompts and human steering workflow.
- [Follow Google’s Gemini CLI game codelab](https://codelabs.developers.google.com/next26/gemini-cli-match3-golang)
- [Download & run Cloud Crush](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/devrel-demos/blob/main/codelabs/gemini-cli/gemini-cli-match3-golang/README.md#local-development) — Local Go / WASM project; no hosted public game endpoint was verified. Use Go 1.26.2+ and run go run . from the game directory. Expand the steps for the complete browser build, asset copy, matching wasm_exec.js, and local server commands. Native play needs a graphical desktop and working audio drivers. Cloud Crush was not compiled locally in this review.
- [Open the complete Go game project](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/devrel-demos/tree/main/codelabs/gemini-cli/gemini-cli-match3-golang) — Includes main.go, source images and audio, go.mod, browser entry and runtime helper, server/main.go, Dockerfile, and publisher screenshots. The repository code is Apache-2.0. A WASM binary must be built locally.

**Study this AI workflow**

1. Download the devrel-demos repository and enter codelabs/gemini-cli/gemini-cli-match3-golang. Install Go 1.26.2 or newer; the README’s 1.24+ prerequisite is outdated. For native desktop play, run: go run .
2. Follow the title and player-name prompts. Use arrow keys to move the cursor and Space to select a gem, then an arrow to swap. Mouse/touch input is also implemented. Compare matching, falling tiles, time bonuses, and score behavior with main.go.
3. For a local browser build, first prepare the files served by the Go server: mkdir -p public/assets; cp assets/* public/assets/; cp index.html public/index.html. The committed public/assets directory is missing source files required by the game, including background.jpg.
4. Use the WASM helper from the same Go installation as the compiler: cp "$(go env GOROOT)/lib/wasm/wasm_exec.js" public/wasm_exec.js. Then compile: GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build -o public/cloud-crush.wasm .
5. Run the browser server from the same game directory: go run server/main.go. Open http://localhost:8080. Local play does not require Gemini CLI, an API key, a Google Cloud account, or cloud deployment.
6. Read the official codelab to trace the development prompts. The browser instructions above were checked against source; this review did not install Go or compile the game. Its preview is a publisher-provided gameplay screenshot.

## Dinosaur Game Offline: Gemini CLI-assisted runner

Jump a pixel dinosaur over cacti and avoid flying obstacles while the score and speed increase. This small browser game includes its complete JavaScript implementation, sprites, and sound effects.

**AI workflow:** The creator explicitly credits Gemini CLI with scaffolding, game logic, debugging, and improvements in the README and game footer. No original conversation or exact model identifier is published; this is a documented assisted build.

- [See the creator’s Gemini CLI disclosure](https://github.com/tonidevvn/dinosaur-game-offline#how-gemini-cli-helped) — README, repository description, and the in-game footer explicitly name gemini-cli. This establishes creator attribution rather than independent proof of fully autonomous generation.
- [Read how Gemini CLI helped](https://github.com/tonidevvn/dinosaur-game-offline#how-gemini-cli-helped)
- [Play Dinosaur Game Offline](https://tonidevvn.github.io/dinosaur-game-offline/) — Author-hosted browser build; earlier catalog notes report a Chromium check, not independently revalidated here. Space starts and jumps; after a collision, click the restart icon. Desktop keyboard recommended because the board has a fixed 900-pixel width. The full project can also run locally by opening index.html.
- [Open the complete dinosaur game source](https://github.com/tonidevvn/dinosaur-game-offline) — Complete index.html, style.css, script.js, and referenced image/audio assets. Public source is available, but the repository does not declare a code license.

**Study this AI workflow**

1. Open the author-hosted browser game on a desktop with a keyboard. Press Space once to start, then press Space again to jump over an approaching cactus.
2. Watch the score rise, test a collision, and use the restart icon after game over. Earlier catalog notes report a start/jump/score/collision/restart smoke test and a preview captured during a jump. That run was not repeated or independently validated in this source-only review.
3. To run locally, download the complete dinosaur-game-offline repository and open index.html. Keep style.css, script.js, and public/ beside it. No npm installation, build step, Gemini CLI, or API key is needed to play.
4. If a browser restricts local files, serve the repository with python3 -m http.server 8080 and open http://localhost:8080. The game board is fixed at 900 pixels wide and targets desktop keyboard play. Its optional Google Fonts stylesheet uses the network.
5. Read the creator’s disclosure, then inspect script.js for the requestAnimationFrame loop, jump state, obstacle spawning, scoring, collision checks, and restart behavior.

## Moonlight & Mayhem

A 3D museum heist made with Codex: rescue two raccoon crewmates, evade security, stack the crew, and steal the Golden Sardine.

**AI workflow:** Simon Willison documents giving Codex the game brief and image-generation access, then requesting a visual bug fix. The published project includes the game, generated textures, and the development transcript.

- [Read the published Codex transcript](https://github.com/simonw/raccoon-heist-codex/blob/main/transcript.md) — The creator links this development record from the build account; it accompanies the game source rather than a generator-only repository.
- [Read the creator’s build and fix log](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/7/moonlight-mayhem/)
- [Play Moonlight & Mayhem](https://simonw.github.io/raccoon-heist-codex/) — Desktop: WASD or arrows to move, E to interact, Space or Shift to dash, Escape to pause. Mobile uses a touch stick and action buttons. Requires a WebGL-capable browser.
- [Open the complete game project](https://github.com/simonw/raccoon-heist-codex/) — Actual game source, committed textures, vendored Three.js, build notes, and transcript. No build step is required; use a local static HTTP server to run the repository.

**Study this AI workflow**

1. Play the heist and trace crew rescue, security detection, interactions, and escape.
2. Read the creator’s build account and compare the original brief with the result.
3. Follow the transcript and commit history to study scene construction, generated art, and the visual bug fix.
4. Serve the complete repository locally, then study one mechanic and its supporting assets.

## TRON: EXONIX

A neon 3D territory-capture game built through Claude Code, Godot MCP, Blender MCP, and generated assets, with human design and playtest feedback.

**AI workflow:** The creator documents Claude writing gameplay, shaders, VFX, and UI while a human steers mechanics and materials. The repository includes the actual Godot game, generated assets, and the asset-generation scripts.

- [Read how the agent workflow was assembled](https://github.com/witnesstodark/tron-exonix/blob/master/CLAUDE.md) — The creator’s reproducible setup record explains the AI’s implementation work, human material review, generation tools, and local launch requirements.
- [Follow the creator’s complete workflow](https://www.top3d.ai/learn/claude-godot-mcp-3d-game)
- [Play TRON: EXONIX](https://www.top3d.ai/demo/exonix-build/index.html) — Creator-hosted Godot web build. Click to enter the grid, press Space to deploy, use the arrow keys to move, and Escape for the menu. A keyboard and a WebGL-capable browser are recommended.
- [Open the complete Godot game project](https://github.com/witnesstodark/tron-exonix) — Includes the Godot project, scripts, shaders, models, textures, audio, and generation scripts. Local play requires Godot 4.7 standard; API access is only needed to regenerate assets.

**Study this AI workflow**

1. Play the web build and study territory capture, trail hazards, enemy movement, and sector progression.
2. Follow the creator’s tutorial from prototype through materials, audio, effects, and web export.
3. Read CLAUDE.md to understand the agent, Godot MCP, Blender review, and asset-generation workflow.
4. Open game/project.godot in Godot 4.7 and press F5; study the scripts alongside the included models, textures, and audio.

## Tetris built by an AI agent team

A complete browser game with a published account of how three Claude Code teammates divided the rules, rendering, and controls.

**AI workflow:** The author documents a Claude Opus 4.6 agent team, shared scaffolding, separate file ownership, and the exact prompts assigned to each teammate.

- [See the original agent prompts](https://github.com/caiguanhao/tetris#the-prompt-used-to-spawn-the-team) — The author publishes the team prompt, individual assignments, model name, and coordination sequence. This is a documented AI-assisted build.
- [Read the agent-team build log](https://github.com/caiguanhao/tetris#built-with-claude-code-agent-teams)
- [Play Tetris](https://caiguanhao.github.io/tetris/) — Browser game with keyboard and touch controls. Press Enter or tap to start.
- [Open the complete game source](https://github.com/caiguanhao/tetris) — Complete HTML, CSS, and JavaScript game, including rules, rendering, controls, procedural music, and sound effects.

**Study this AI workflow**

1. Play the finished game and test rotation, hard drop, pause, and restart.
2. Read the original team prompt and the separate engine, renderer, and UI assignments.
3. Compare the shared state and event contract with each teammate’s completed module.
4. Review the coordination notes to see how parallel work was assigned and integrated.

## Tower of Time: prompting a rewind mechanic

A finished tower-defense game with time reversal and an extensive author-published prompt log covering mechanics, debugging, and polish.

**AI workflow:** The author used Augment Code and Cursor agents, mainly with Claude Sonnet 4, while also editing code and arranging scenes in Phaser Editor.

- [Read the AI contribution disclosure](https://github.com/maciej-trebacz/tower-of-time-game#vibe-coding-proof-of-concept) — The author describes the AI tools used; the prompt log explicitly discloses manual code edits and scene work in Phaser Editor.
- [Read the author’s prompt log](https://github.com/maciej-trebacz/tower-of-time-game/blob/main/PROMPTS.md)
- [Play Tower of Time](https://m4v3k.itch.io/tower-of-time) — Choose Run game, then Start. Use arrow keys to move, Space for actions, and Backspace to rewind; gamepad controls are also available.
- [Open the complete game project](https://github.com/maciej-trebacz/tower-of-time-game) — Complete Phaser and TypeScript project with scenes, gameplay systems, image assets, music, sound effects, font files, and asset credits.

**Study this AI workflow**

1. Play the game and try building defenses, surviving waves, and rewinding time.
2. Read the Rewindable Sprite prompts and the follow-up reports that refine the mechanic.
3. Trace how the author supplied file context, documentation, and observed errors to the agents.
4. Compare the prompt history with the complete project, including scenes, gameplay systems, and assets.

## AI production tools and frameworks

A tool interface, recorded video, model, SDK, and complete game are different deliverables. Source scope is stated below.

### AutoUE

Coordinates agents to build Unreal scenes, gameplay code, interactions, and playtests.

- **Tutorial (tutorial):** [Setup and usage](https://github.com/Pluto156/AutoUE#setup-and-usage). Author instructions for dependencies, service credentials, and running the Unreal generation pipeline.
- **Demo (video):** [Game-generation video](https://github.com/Pluto156/AutoUE/blob/main/assets/show.mp4). Recorded demonstrations of generated Unreal games; no public browser-playable build verified.
- **Source (pipeline-source):** [Pipeline source](https://github.com/Pluto156/AutoUE). Public framework implementation; engine setup, model services, and dataset assets remain separate requirements.

### UniGen

Plans Unity prototypes, generates scripts, assembles scenes, and supports iterative debugging.

- **Tutorial (tutorial):** [Installation and usage](https://github.com/yxwan123/UniGen#-installation). README covers prerequisites and the local Unity generation workflow; review paths and project setup before running.
- **Demo (video):** [Unity generation video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xyJjFfnxUx0). Author-linked demonstration video, not a browser-playable game.
- **Source (pipeline-source):** [Pipeline source](https://github.com/yxwan123/UniGen). Published generator implementation and prompts; this is not a complete release of every benchmark game.

### Scenario

Builds consistent game art pipelines with custom style models and batch generation.

- **Tutorial (tutorial):** [Consistent game asset pipeline](https://docs.scenario.com/get-started/documentation/integrating-with-applications-real-world-scenarios#1-game-asset-pipeline--batch-generation-with-style-consistency). Official walkthrough for custom style training, batch generation, and asset delivery.
- **Demo (interactive):** [Asset generation app](https://app.scenario.com/). Hosted creative tool requiring an account; this is an asset workspace, not a playable game.
- **Source (sdk):** [Unity integration source](https://github.com/scenario-labs/Scenario-Unity). Public Unity integration plugin; hosted model source and a complete game project are not included.

### Meshy API

Connects AI model generation, humanoid rigging, and animation export for game asset workflows.

- **Tutorial (tutorial):** [Image to animated character](https://www.meshy.ai/developers/cookbook/recipes/animate-3d-character/). Official guide with reference files, Python and TypeScript examples, and GLB/FBX outputs. API access uses credits.
- **Demo (interactive):** [3D asset workspace](https://www.meshy.ai/workspace). Hosted generation and animation workspace; account access is required to generate assets. This is not a playable game.
- **Source (examples):** [Cookbook example source](https://github.com/meshy-dev/meshy-cookbook). Public asset-generation recipes, not Meshy's model source or a complete game project.

### HY-Motion 1.0

Generates skeletal humanoid motion from text with public inference code and model weights.

- **Tutorial (tutorial):** [Installation and motion workflow](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HY-Motion-1.0/blob/master/README.md). Official setup, CLI inference, local UI, and prompting guidance. Local execution requires the documented GPU resources.
- **Demo (interactive):** [Interactive motion demo](https://huggingface.co/spaces/tencent/HY-Motion-1.0). Official text-to-motion model interface; a motion preview rather than playable gameplay. Hosted availability may vary.
- **Source (model):** [Motion implementation source](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HY-Motion-1.0). Public inference and visualization implementation with separately linked weights; no complete game project.

### ElevenLabs Sound Effects

Generates game sound effects, Foley, and looping ambience from text through a web app or API.

- **Tutorial (tutorial):** [Sound Effects quickstart](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/cookbooks/sound-effects). Official API walkthrough with SDK examples; an account and API key are needed for generation.
- **Demo (interactive):** [Sound effects generator](https://elevenlabs.io/sound-effects). Official text-to-audio generator and sound examples; this is an audio tool, not a playable game.
- **Source (sdk):** [Official Python SDK](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python). API client source only; generation model and complete game source are not included.

### Stable Audio Open 1.0

Provides downloadable text-to-audio weights and local tools for sound effects and field recordings.

- **Tutorial (tutorial):** [Local inference and WAV export](https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-audio-open-1.0#usage). Official model usage examples for stable-audio-tools and Diffusers.
- **Demo (local-tool):** [Local audio demo setup](https://github.com/Stability-AI/stable-audio-tools#interface). Download and run the official Gradio audio interface locally; this link is setup guidance, not a hosted playable game.
- **Source (model):** [Audio tools source](https://github.com/Stability-AI/stable-audio-tools). Public training and inference tools with separately downloadable model weights; no complete game project.

### Regression Games

Provides a public Unity SDK for gameplay recording, input replay, and regression-test reference workflows.

- **Tutorial (tutorial):** [Your first automated test](https://github.com/Regression-Games/RegressionDocs/blob/main/docs/getting-started/creating-your-first-automated-test.mdx). Official first-test walkthrough preserved in the documentation repository. The former live documentation domain was unreachable during review.
- **Demo (examples):** [Runnable Boss Room sample](https://github.com/Regression-Games/UITest-BossRoom). A complete Unity sample project with UI tests; download and open locally rather than playing in a browser.
- **Source (sdk):** [Unity testing SDK source](https://github.com/Regression-Games/RGUnityBots). Public client SDK source; it does not contain the complete hosted dashboard backend.

### modl.ai

Uses visual agents and natural-language tasks to test uploaded game builds.

- **Tutorial (service):** [Workflow overview](https://modl.ai/). Official upload, task-definition, and reporting overview; detailed onboarding is provided through the service.
- **Demo (service):** [Book a product demo](https://modl.ai/contact). Commercial demonstration by arrangement; this is not a public playable game or instant sandbox.
- **Source (unavailable):** Full product source unavailable. No complete source release for the current hosted testing product was verified; older public samples are not its backend.

### Convai

Adds conversational NPCs with speech, memory, emotion, and in-scene actions.

- **Tutorial (tutorial):** [Build your first AI character](https://docs.convai.com/api-docs/plugins-and-integrations/convai-unity-sdk/getting-started). Official Unity installation, service setup, sample-scene, and custom-character walkthrough.
- **Demo (interactive):** [Try character experiences](https://x.convai.com/). Account-required browser character experiences; these are conversations and role-play, not complete game-generation demos.
- **Source (sdk):** [Unreal engine SDK source](https://github.com/Conv-AI/Convai-UnrealEngine-SDK-V4). Public engine integration source; the complete cloud conversation service is not included.

## Additional asset-to-game workflow

The [Tripo Vibe Gaming Interactive Playbook](https://github.com/TripoGrowthLab/vibe-gaming-interactive-playbook) publishes a staged AI coding and generated-model workflow with playable 3D examples. Its public game code runs with greybox objects because the Tripo model files are not bundled. It is useful production guidance, but is not counted among the featured complete game-and-asset projects above.

Source review and browser smoke testing do not establish full reproduction, complete gameplay coverage, or the availability of every third-party service.
